t: The Gospels of Matthew and Luke describe Mary as a virgin chosen by God to conceive Jesus through the Holy Spirit, and they place her at the birth of Jesus, in Nazareth, and at his crucifixion.
Little is recorded of her life: the Bible does not describe her death, and the later accounts of her parents, childhood and end are scholars' and churches' traditions rather than firm history.
Churches differ widely over her: Catholics and the Orthodox hold distinctive beliefs and devotions, most Protestants honour her without venerating her, and the Quran gives her a chapter of her own.
dyk: Mary is the only woman named in the Quran, which mentions or refers to her 50 times and gives one chapter her name, while the earliest known prayer to her, the Sub tuum praesidium, was found on a papyrus in Egypt in 1917.
ev: Mary, betrothed to Joseph, is told by the angel Gabriel that she will conceive Jesus through the Holy Spirit, as Luke tells it
She gives birth to Jesus in Bethlehem, according to Luke during a Roman census, and presents him at the Temple in Jerusalem
At her suggestion Jesus works his first miracle at the wedding at Cana, in the Gospel of John
She stands near the cross at the crucifixion of Jesus, in John's account
Acts names her with the apostles and the brothers of Jesus in the upper room after the Ascension
The Council of Ephesus declares her Theotokos, the God-bearer
Pope Pius IX proclaims the Immaculate Conception
Pope Pius XII defines the Assumption in Munificentissimus Deus

f.born: Date not recorded; a Jewish woman of Nazareth in Galilee, betrothed to Joseph; the Gospel of James, a later text, names her parents as Joachim and Anne
f.died: Not recorded in the Bible; Hyppolitus of Thebes, writing in the 7th or 8th century, says she died in 41 CE; Orthodox tradition holds that she died naturally (the Dormition) and was then taken bodily into Heaven
f.role: Mother of Jesus and wife of Joseph; held by Eastern and Oriental Orthodox, Catholic, Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican and Methodist churches to be the Mother of God; historians know her chiefly through the Gospels and Acts
f.known: the annunciation by the angel Gabriel; the birth of Jesus at Bethlehem; presence at the wedding at Cana and at the crucifixion; the Magnificat; Theotokos, proclaimed at the Council of Ephesus in 431; the Assumption; the only woman named in the Quran
